subject: MSA & Order Form — maintenance window timing, credit trigger, and response ladder
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stellarai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellarai.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — uptime / maintenance / credits (StellarAI)

Kimberly — thanks again for the call earlier. We reviewed the MSA/Order Form redlines your team returned and have a few follow-ups focused on operational guarantees before we can loop in our legal for final sign-off. Primary asks from our side: (1) confirm target uptime (we're asking for 99.95% across the hosted API), (2) simplify the credit schedule so it's tiered but predictable, and (3) tighten the P1/P2 response windows to reflect our customer SLAs.

Quick context: our traffic profile is bursty (EOD batch writes plus synchronous inference for UI), so short tail latency and clear maintenance windows are important. Can your team confirm whether the maintenance window definition in Section 5.4 can be limited to 8 hours/month (vs the broad wording in your draft)? Also attaching our internal uptime expectations matrix for reference (attached: uptime_matrix.xlsx).

If helpful, we can take a very short redline and mark the clauses we'd want legal to accept. Appreciate a suggested compromise you can take to your ops/engineering partners.

—Alex
Director, Infrastructure — StellarAI
Attachment: uptime_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stellarai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — uptime / maintenance / credits (StellarAI)

Alex — thanks for the clear asks and the matrix, that helps. I've looped in Ben (Support/Oncall) and Naomi (Contracts) to weigh in on the operational feasibility and the business impact. Initial reactions:

- Uptime target: We typically offer 99.9% as a baseline for hosted public APIs. 99.95% is achievable for Dedicated capacity or with SLA add-ons (reserved capacity + additional monitoring + guaranteed slot allocation). If StellarAI needs 99.95 for the hosted product, that would carry a contract amendment and pricing delta.

- Maintenance window: Happy to tighten the language. We can agree to a defined maintenance budget (e.g., up to 8 hours/month for planned maintenance) provided we include a small carveout for emergency hotfixes and security patches (we propose: 8 hours/month planned + up to 2 unplanned emergency hours per quarter, with prior notice when possible).

- Credit schedule: Our preference is a staircase credit model tied to calendar month availability (credits as % of monthly invoice). We can map Alex's requested tiers to a compromise. I'll attach a one-page counterproposal (redline_MSA_v3.docx) with sample numbers for monthly credits and the trigger math so legal can see the arithmetic.

Ben — can you confirm that P1 response (acknowledge within 15 minutes, engineer engaged within 60 minutes, and mitigation plan within 4 hours) is workable for the customer's expected tiers, or do we need to reserve that for Dedicated commitments?

Alex — we'll aim to circulate the redline + explicit pricing lift for 99.95 by EOD Thursday. If Stellar's procurement can accept the Dedicated/Reserved language, we can expedite commitment and provisioning.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations (procurement liaison)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_MSA_v3.docx (docx)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@stellarai.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — uptime / maintenance / credits (StellarAI)

Alex / Kimberly — quick operational notes from the support side:

- Response ladder: For hosted customers on standard plans we provide: P1: 15m ack / 60m engineer engage / 4h mitigation plan. P2: 1h ack / 4h engineer / 24h mitigation. For Dedicated customers we can commit to faster engineering SLAs (P1: 10m ack / 30m engineer). If StellarAI requires the faster Dedicated ladder, that will be part of the capacity commitment.

- Maintenance blackout periods: We can honor two rolling 7-day blackout windows per quarter if you sign a 12-month commitment and provide 7 days' notice for planned cutovers. We cannot guarantee zero impact during provider-level emergencies; those are excluded per Section 5.4 but we will publish an incident transparency report within 24h.

- Credit math: We'll propose a proportional credit (monthly invoice * %), with a floor so the credits don't exceed a practical cap. For example: 99.9–99.0% = 10% credit, 98.99–95.0% = 25% credit, <95% = 50% credit — we can adjust boundaries. We prefer not to make credits automatic for scheduled maintenance that's notified 72h in advance.

If you can confirm which product tier you'll be on (Hosted Standard vs Dedicated Reserved), I can finalize the exact numbers and delivery playbook.

—Ben
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stellarai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellarai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — uptime / maintenance / credits (StellarAI)

Kimberly / Ben — thank you, that level of detail is exactly what we needed. Quick answers from our side:

- We're prepared to pilot on Hosted Standard for Q4 but require 99.95 for our customer-facing endpoints. If Redwood can offer a clear pricing adder for a 99.95 SLA on Hosted (rather than mandating Dedicated), we'd prefer that path to avoid procurement hoops. Please include the Price delta per vCPU/GPU and monthly minimums in the redline.

- Maintenance: we accept the 8 hours/month planned + 2 emergency hours/quarter carveout as a reasonable compromise. Please ensure planned maintenance notifications are at least 72h (48h at minimum if critical).

- Credits: the staircase model is fine; one request — can you table the exact percentage values in the redline and give an example calculation? The example will help our finance team sign off quickly.

Next steps: We'll review the redline_MSA_v3.docx and the uptime math. If everything aligns, we'll push to legal this week. Could you also attach a one-page summary that we can share with our procurement and finance leads?

Thanks again — Alex
Director, Infrastructure — StellarAI
